meaning: For the whole day.
cue: Say why you are tired this evening.
reply: I worked in the garden all day.
replyJapanese: 一日中、庭仕事をしていました。
transferCue: Describe the weather on your day off.
transferReply: It rained all day on Sunday.
transferReplyJapanese: 日曜日は一日中、雨でした。
nuance: Say all day, not all the day. It usually goes at the end of the sentence.
nuanceJapanese: all the day とは言わず、all day と言う。ふつう文末に置く。

meaning: Good enough, or with no problems.
japanese: まあまあよい。問題ない。
cue: A friend asks about the film you saw.
reply: The film was all right, but a bit long.
replyJapanese: 映画はまあまあでしたが、少し長かったです。
transferCue: A waiter checks on your table.
transferReply: Is everything all right with your meal?
transferReplyJapanese: お食事に何か問題はございませんか？
nuance: Write two words in careful writing; alright is informal. It means quite good, not very good.
nuanceJapanese: きちんとした文章では2語で書く。alright はくだけた綴り。「とてもよい」ではなく「まあまあよい」という意味。

meaning: In the place where you live.
cue: A friend phones and asks where you are.
reply: I'm at home with the kids today.
replyJapanese: 今日は子どもたちと家にいます。
transferCue: Explain why you got wet in the rain.
transferReply: I left my umbrella at home this morning.
transferReplyJapanese: 今朝、傘を家に置いてきてしまいました。
nuance: No article: at home, not at the home. After go or come, drop at: go home.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない（at the home は誤り）。go や come のあとでは at を取って go home と言う。

meaning: Doing your job, usually at the place where you work.
cue: Someone phones and asks for your mother.
reply: She's at work until six today.
replyJapanese: 母は今日、6時まで仕事です。
transferCue: Say why you did not answer a message.
transferReply: Sorry, I was at work all morning.
transferReplyJapanese: すみません、午前中はずっと仕事でした。
nuance: No article: at work, not at the work. Use go to work for the journey there.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない（at the work は誤り）。職場へ向かうことは go to work と言う。

meaning: Do the work a teacher gives you to do at home.
cue: A child wants to watch TV after school.
reply: Do your homework first, then you can watch TV.
replyJapanese: 先に宿題をしてくださいね。そのあとならテレビを見ていいですよ。
transferCue: Say how you used your time on the way to school.
transferReply: I did my homework on the bus this morning.
transferReplyJapanese: 今朝、バスの中で宿題をしました。
nuance: Use do, never make. Homework cannot be counted: a lot of homework, not homeworks.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞は do を使い、make は使わない。homework は数えられない名詞で、homeworks とはしない（a lot of homework）。

meaning: Used to politely get someone's attention.
japanese: すみません。ちょっとよろしいですか。
cue: Ask a stranger on a train about a seat.
reply: Excuse me, is this seat free?
replyJapanese: すみません、この席は空いていますか？
transferCue: Call a waiter to your table.
transferReply: Excuse me, could we have some water, please?
transferReplyJapanese: すみません、お水をいただけますか？
nuance: Say it before you speak to a stranger. If you bump into someone, British speakers say sorry; Americans often say excuse me.
nuanceJapanese: 知らない人に話しかける前に言う。人にぶつかったとき、イギリスでは sorry、アメリカでは excuse me と言うことが多い。

meaning: Used to give an example of what you mean.
cue: Say what kind of sweet food you like.
reply: I like cold desserts, for example ice cream.
replyJapanese: 冷たいデザートが好きです。たとえばアイスクリームです。
transferCue: Suggest a day to meet a colleague.
transferReply: We could meet next week, for example on Tuesday.
transferReplyJapanese: 来週、たとえば火曜日に会うのはどうでしょうか。
nuance: Put a comma before it, and after it when it starts a sentence. For instance means the same; e.g. is the short written form.
nuanceJapanese: 前にコンマを置き、文頭ならあとにもコンマを置く。for instance も同じ意味で、書くときは e.g. と略すこともある。

meaning: Put on your clothes.
cue: Describe the start of your morning.
reply: I get dressed before I have breakfast.
replyJapanese: 朝食の前に着替えます。
transferCue: Hurry a child who is late for school.
transferReply: Please get dressed now. The bus leaves at eight.
transferReplyJapanese: もう着替えてください。バスは8時に出ますよ。
nuance: It takes no object. For one piece of clothing use put on: put on a coat. The opposite is get undressed.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は取らない。衣類を1つ身につけるときは put on を使う（put on a coat）。反対は get undressed。

meaning: Prepare yourself for something.
japanese: 準備をする。支度をする。
cue: Friends are waiting to leave for dinner.
reply: Give me ten minutes to get ready.
replyJapanese: 支度するので、10分待ってください。
transferCue: Describe the evening before a holiday.
transferReply: We got ready for the trip last night.
transferReplyJapanese: 昨夜のうちに旅行の準備をしました。
frame: Get ready for something / to do something
nuance: Use for before a noun and to before a verb: get ready for school, get ready to go.
nuanceJapanese: 名詞の前は for、動詞の前は to を使う（get ready for school / get ready to go）。

meaning: Walk somewhere for pleasure.
cue: Suggest something to do after lunch.
reply: Let's go for a walk in the park.
replyJapanese: 公園へ散歩に行きましょう。
transferCue: Describe your grandfather's morning habit.
transferReply: He goes for a walk every morning at six.
transferReplyJapanese: 祖父は毎朝6時に散歩に出かけます。
nuance: Keep for and a: not go to walk. Americans also say take a walk.
nuanceJapanese: for と a を落とさない（go to walk は誤り）。アメリカ英語では take a walk とも言う。

meaning: Go to shops to look at and buy things.
cue: A friend asks about your weekend plans.
reply: I'm going shopping with my sister on Saturday.
replyJapanese: 土曜日は姉と買い物に行きます。
transferCue: Explain where your parents are.
transferReply: They went shopping for a new sofa.
transferReplyJapanese: 両親は新しいソファを買いに出かけました。
nuance: No to before shopping: go shopping, not go to shopping. For food you can also say do the shopping.
nuanceJapanese: shopping の前に to は入れない（go to shopping は誤り）。食料品の買い物は do the shopping とも言う。

meaning: Get into your bed to sleep.
cue: Someone asks about your usual evening.
reply: I usually go to bed at eleven.
replyJapanese: たいてい11時に寝ます。
transferCue: Say why you missed a late message.
transferReply: Sorry, I went to bed early last night.
transferReplyJapanese: すみません、昨夜は早く寝てしまいました。
nuance: No the: go to bed, not go to the bed. It means getting into bed; fall asleep is when sleep starts.
nuanceJapanese: the は付けない（go to the bed は誤り）。床に入ることを指し、眠りに落ちる瞬間は fall asleep と言う。

meaning: Used to wish someone success.
japanese: がんばって。幸運を祈ります。
cue: A friend has a driving test tomorrow.
reply: Good luck with your driving test tomorrow!
replyJapanese: 明日の運転免許の試験、がんばってください！
transferCue: Your sister is leaving for a job interview.
transferReply: Good luck, and call me after the interview.
transferReplyJapanese: がんばってください。面接が終わったら電話してくださいね。
nuance: Use with before a noun: good luck with your exam. No article: not a good luck.
nuanceJapanese: 名詞の前には with を使う（good luck with your exam）。冠詞は付けず、a good luck とは言わない。

meaning: Enjoy yourself.
japanese: 楽しむ。楽しい時間を過ごす。
cue: Your brother is leaving for a party.
reply: Have fun at the party tonight!
replyJapanese: 今夜のパーティー、楽しんできてくださいね！
transferCue: Describe a winter day with your family.
transferReply: The children had fun in the snow yesterday.
transferReplyJapanese: 子どもたちは昨日、雪の中で楽しく遊びました。
nuance: No article: have fun, not have a fun. To make it stronger, say have lots of fun.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない（have a fun は誤り）。強めるときは have lots of fun と言う。

meaning: Used when you give something to someone.
cue: Give a customer their change in a shop.
reply: Here you are, that's two pounds change.
replyJapanese: はい、どうぞ。2ポンドのお釣りです。
transferCue: A classmate asks to borrow a pen.
transferReply: Here you are. You can keep it.
transferReplyJapanese: はい、どうぞ。返さなくていいですよ。
nuance: Say it as you hand the thing over. Here you go is more casual; here it is means you have found something.
nuanceJapanese: 物を手渡しながら言う。here you go はよりくだけた言い方。here it is は探し物を見つけたときの表現。

meaning: Used to suggest something.
cue: Friends cannot decide what to eat.
reply: How about pizza for dinner tonight?
replyJapanese: 今夜の夕食はピザにしませんか？
transferCue: Suggest a time for a meeting.
transferReply: How about meeting at ten on Monday?
transferReplyJapanese: 月曜日の10時に会うのはどうですか？
nuance: Follow it with a noun or an -ing form: how about going, not how about to go. What about means the same.
nuanceJapanese: あとには名詞か -ing 形を置く（how about to go は誤り）。what about も同じ意味。

meaning: Become friends with someone.
japanese: 友だちになる。友だちを作る。
cue: A parent asks about your first week at a new school.
reply: I made friends with two girls in my class.
replyJapanese: クラスの女の子2人と友だちになりました。
transferCue: Describe someone who is very sociable.
transferReply: My brother makes friends easily wherever he goes.
transferReplyJapanese: 弟はどこへ行っても、すぐに友だちができます。
nuance: Friends is always plural, even with one person: make friends with him. Use with before the person.
nuanceJapanese: 相手が1人でも friends は複数形（make friends with him）。相手の前には with を置く。

meaning: Used to say you can easily do what someone asks.
japanese: いいですよ。お安いご用です。
cue: A colleague asks you to send a file again.
reply: No problem, I'll send it again now.
replyJapanese: いいですよ、今もう一度送ります。
transferCue: A neighbour asks you to water her plants.
transferReply: No problem. I can do it every morning.
transferReplyJapanese: 大丈夫ですよ。毎朝やっておきます。
nuance: Friendly and informal. It is also a common answer to thank you, like you're welcome.
nuanceJapanese: 親しみのあるくだけた返事。thank you への返事にもなり、you're welcome と同じ働きをする。

meaning: Used to say yes or to give permission.
cue: A guest asks to use your phone charger.
reply: Of course, it's on the kitchen table.
replyJapanese: もちろんです。台所のテーブルの上にありますよ。
transferCue: A friend asks if you will come to her wedding.
transferReply: Of course I'm coming to your wedding!
transferReplyJapanese: もちろん、結婚式には行きますよ！
nuance: Warm as an answer to a request. As an answer to a question about facts it can sound like you should know that.
nuanceJapanese: 頼みごとへの返事なら温かく響く。事実を尋ねる質問への返事に使うと「知っていて当然でしょう」と聞こえることがある。

meaning: At the present time.
cue: A colleague asks if you can talk.
reply: I'm busy right now, but I'm free after lunch.
replyJapanese: 今は手が離せませんが、昼食のあとなら空いています。
transferCue: A friend asks where your brother lives.
transferReply: He's living in Osaka right now.
transferReplyJapanese: 兄は今、大阪に住んでいます。
nuance: Often used with be + -ing. It is stronger and more informal than now, and it can also mean immediately.
nuanceJapanese: be + -ing とよく一緒に使う。now より強く、くだけた言い方。「今すぐ」の意味にもなる。

meaning: Tell someone goodbye when you or they leave.
japanese: 別れのあいさつをする。さよならを言う。
cue: You are about to leave a friend's house.
reply: Wait, I want to say goodbye to your parents.
replyJapanese: ちょっと待ってください。ご両親にあいさつしてから帰りたいんです。
transferCue: Describe the last day of primary school.
transferReply: We said goodbye to our teacher and cried.
transferReplyJapanese: 先生にお別れを言って、みんなで泣きました。
nuance: Use to before the person: say goodbye to her, not say her goodbye. Say bye is more casual.
nuanceJapanese: 相手の前には to を置く（say goodbye to her）。say her goodbye とは言わない。say bye はよりくだけた形。

meaning: Greet someone.
japanese: あいさつする。よろしくと伝える。
cue: You see a neighbour across the street.
reply: Let's go and say hello to Mrs Tanaka.
replyJapanese: 田中さんにあいさつしに行きましょう。
transferCue: A friend is about to visit her family.
transferReply: Say hello to your mum for me.
transferReplyJapanese: お母さんによろしく伝えてくださいね。
nuance: Use to before the person. Say hello to someone for me asks a person to pass on your greeting. Say hi is more casual.
nuanceJapanese: 相手の前には to を置く。say hello to ... for me は「よろしく伝えて」という頼み方。say hi はよりくだけた形。

meaning: Used to say goodbye in a friendly way.
japanese: じゃあ、また。またあとで。
cue: You leave the office for lunch.
reply: I'm going for lunch. See you later!
replyJapanese: お昼に行ってきます。ではまたあとで！
transferCue: End a phone call with a friend.
transferReply: I have to go now, see you later.
transferReplyJapanese: もう切らないと。じゃあ、またね。
nuance: Informal. People say it even when they have no plan to meet later that day.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた別れのあいさつ。その日のうちにまた会う予定がなくても使う。

meaning: Used to say goodbye to someone you will meet again soon.
cue: A friend will fly to visit you next week.
reply: Have a safe trip, and see you soon!
replyJapanese: 気をつけて来てくださいね。では、また近いうちに！
transferCue: End a message to a classmate before term starts.
transferReply: School starts on Monday, so see you soon.
transferReplyJapanese: 月曜日から学校だね。じゃあ、またすぐに。
nuance: Use it when you expect to meet again before long. For a fixed day, say see you on Friday or see you tomorrow.
nuanceJapanese: 近いうちにまた会うと分かっているときに使う。日が決まっているなら see you on Friday や see you tomorrow と言う。

meaning: Be careful so that nothing goes wrong.
cue: The roads are icy and a friend is driving home.
reply: Take care on the roads tonight.
replyJapanese: 今夜は道路に気をつけてくださいね。
transferCue: Someone is cutting bread with your new knife.
transferReply: Take care with that knife. It's very sharp.
transferReplyJapanese: その包丁には気をつけてください。とてもよく切れます。
nuance: No article: take care, not take a care. Said alone, Take care! is also a friendly goodbye.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない（take a care は誤り）。単独の Take care! は親しい別れのあいさつにもなる。

meaning: Used to praise someone for doing something well.
cue: A pupil gets full marks in a spelling test.
reply: Well done, you got every word right!
replyJapanese: よくできました。全部正解ですよ！
transferCue: A colleague gave a good talk.
transferReply: Well done on your talk this morning.
transferReplyJapanese: 今朝の発表、とてもよかったですよ。
nuance: Mainly British; Americans more often say good job. It is praise from above, so it can sound odd said to your boss.
nuanceJapanese: 主にイギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では good job が多い。目上から目下へのほめ言葉なので、上司に言うと不自然になりやすい。

meaning: Used as a polite answer when someone thanks you.
cue: A tourist thanks you for showing the way.
reply: You're welcome. Enjoy your day in the city!
replyJapanese: どういたしまして。街での一日を楽しんでくださいね！
transferCue: A friend thanks you for a lift to the station.
transferReply: You're welcome, it was on my way.
transferReplyJapanese: どういたしまして。通り道でしたから。
nuance: Spell it you're, not your. No problem is a more casual answer to thanks.
nuanceJapanese: 綴りは your ではなく you're。no problem はよりくだけた返事。

meaning: Pay attention to a sound or to what someone says.
japanese: 注意して聞く。耳を傾ける。
cue: Say what you do on the way to work.
reply: I listen to the news on the train.
replyJapanese: 電車の中でニュースを聞きます。
transferCue: A teacher starts the lesson.
transferReply: Please listen to me carefully, everyone.
transferReplyJapanese: みなさん、私の話をよく聞いてください。
nuance: Never drop to before an object: listen to music, not listen music. With no object, say just listen.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語の前の to を落とさない（listen music は誤り）。目的語がなければ listen だけで使う。
contrast: Listen to means paying attention on purpose; hear means a sound simply reaches your ears.
contrastJapanese: listen to は意識して耳を傾けること。hear は音が自然に耳に入ること。

meaning: Have someone or something in your mind.
japanese: 〜のことを思う。思い浮かべる。
cue: Write to a friend who moved abroad last year.
reply: I often think about you and your family.
replyJapanese: あなたとご家族のことをよく思い出します。
transferCue: Someone sees you looking out of the window.
transferReply: I was thinking about our holiday in Spain.
transferReplyJapanese: スペインでの休暇のことを考えていました。
nuance: Often used in the -ing form: I was thinking about you. A verb after about also takes -ing: think about moving.
nuanceJapanese: -ing 形でよく使う（I was thinking about you）。about のあとに動詞が来るときも -ing 形にする（think about moving）。
contrast: Think about keeps something in your mind for a while; think of often means it comes to mind suddenly.
contrastJapanese: think about はしばらく頭の中で思いめぐらすこと。think of はふと頭に浮かぶときによく使う。

meaning: Despite what you expected or planned before.
cue: The forecast said rain, but the picnic went well.
reply: It didn't rain after all, so we ate outside.
replyJapanese: 結局雨は降らなかったので、外で食べました。
transferCue: You said no to an invitation, but your plans changed.
transferReply: I can come to your party after all.
transferReplyJapanese: やっぱりパーティーに行けることになりました。
nuance: In this meaning it goes at the end of the sentence. Do not use it to mean finally; that is at last.
nuanceJapanese: この意味では文末に置く。「ついに」の意味では使わない（それは at last）。

meaning: Used to politely let someone go before you.
cue: You and a stranger reach a door together.
reply: After you. I'm not in a hurry.
replyJapanese: お先にどうぞ。急いでいませんので。
transferCue: You and a colleague both reach for the coffee pot.
transferReply: After you. I'm still looking for my cup.
transferReplyJapanese: お先にどうぞ。私はまだカップを探しているので。
nuance: Usually said alone, with a small hand gesture. Go ahead is a more casual way to say the same thing.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう単独で、軽く手で示しながら言う。go ahead はよりくだけた同じ意味の表現。

meaning: Many times.
japanese: 何度も何度も。繰り返し。
cue: Say how you learned the words of a song.
reply: I listened to the song again and again.
replyJapanese: その曲を何度も繰り返し聞きました。
transferCue: Report a software problem to a colleague.
transferReply: The same error appears again and again.
transferReplyJapanese: 同じエラーが何度も繰り返し出ます。
nuance: It goes after the verb or at the end of the sentence. It stresses the repetition more than often does. Over and over means the same.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞のあとか文末に置く。often より繰り返しを強く表す。over and over も同じ意味。

meaning: Used to stress that you could do something for a very long time.
japanese: いつまででも。一日中でも。
cue: Say how much you enjoy a friend's cooking.
reply: I could eat your pasta all day long.
replyJapanese: あなたのパスタなら、いつまででも食べていられます。
transferCue: Describe someone who loves one subject.
transferReply: She can talk about her dogs all day long.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は犬の話なら一日中でもしていられます。
frame: Could do something all day long
nuance: Often used with can or could to show how much you enjoy something. It can also simply mean for the whole day.
nuanceJapanese: can や could とともに使い、どれほど好きかを強調することが多い。文字どおり「一日中ずっと」の意味でも使う。

meaning: Used to wish someone well when you say goodbye.
japanese: お元気で。ご多幸を祈ります。
cue: A colleague is leaving for a new job.
reply: All the best in your new job, Maria.
replyJapanese: マリアさん、新しい職場でのご活躍を祈っています。
transferCue: End a birthday message to an old friend.
transferReply: All the best to you and your family.
transferReplyJapanese: あなたとご家族のご多幸をお祈りします。
frame: All the best in / with something
nuance: Friendly, for people you know quite well. It can also end an email, written alone on a line above your name.
nuanceJapanese: ある程度親しい相手に使う、親しみのある表現。メールの結びとして、名前の上に単独で1行に書くこともできる。

meaning: Very often, or without stopping.
cue: Describe the weather where you live.
reply: It rains all the time in my town.
replyJapanese: 私の町ではしょっちゅう雨が降ります。
transferCue: Explain why your tablet battery is low.
transferReply: My son plays games on it all the time.
transferReplyJapanese: 息子がいつもそれでゲームをしているんです。
nuance: It goes after the verb or at the end, not before the verb like always. It can sound like a complaint.
nuanceJapanese: always と違って動詞の前ではなく、動詞のあとか文末に置く。不満の響きになることもある。

meaning: Completely, or as much as possible.
cue: The room is hot and the window is only half open.
reply: Can you open the window all the way?
replyJapanese: 窓を全開にしてもらえますか？
transferCue: A friend is nervous about changing jobs.
transferReply: I'll support you all the way.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後までずっと応援しますよ。
nuance: It goes after the verb and its object. With to and a place it means the whole distance: all the way to the station.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞と目的語のあとに置く。to と場所を続けると「〜までずっと」という距離の意味になる（all the way to the station）。

meaning: As quickly as you can.
cue: A customer is waiting for an answer.
reply: Please reply to her as soon as possible.
replyJapanese: 彼女にできるだけ早く返信してください。
transferCue: Phone the dentist about a bad tooth.
transferReply: I'd like an appointment as soon as possible, please.
transferReplyJapanese: できるだけ早い予約をお願いしたいのですが。
frame: Do something as soon as possible
nuance: In emails it is often shortened to ASAP. As an order it can sound pushy, so add please or give a date.
nuanceJapanese: メールでは ASAP と略すことが多い。命令として使うと押しつけがましく響くので、please を添えるか期日を示す。

meaning: In the way that happens most of the time.
japanese: いつものように。相変わらず。
cue: Explain why you arrived late again.
reply: The bus was late as usual this morning.
replyJapanese: 今朝もいつものようにバスが遅れました。
transferCue: Describe the start of the weekly team meeting.
transferReply: As usual, Ken arrived first and made the coffee.
transferReplyJapanese: いつものとおり、ケンさんが最初に来てコーヒーをいれました。
nuance: Say as usual, not as usually. It goes at the start or the end of the sentence.
nuanceJapanese: as usually とは言わない。文頭か文末に置く。

meaning: In addition; too.
cue: Add something to your order in a café.
reply: I'll have a coffee and a sandwich as well.
replyJapanese: コーヒーと、サンドイッチもお願いします。
transferCue: Ask whether a colleague is joining the office trip.
transferReply: Is Tom coming on the trip as well?
transferReplyJapanese: トムさんも旅行に来るのですか？
nuance: It goes at the end of the sentence. It is most common in British English; too is used everywhere. In negatives use either.
nuanceJapanese: 文末に置く。イギリス英語で特によく使い、too はどこでも使われる。否定文では either を使う。

meaning: Used to make a negative sentence or a question stronger.
japanese: まったく（〜ない）。少しでも。
cue: A friend asks if you liked the film.
reply: I didn't like the ending at all.
replyJapanese: 結末がまったく気に入りませんでした。
transferCue: A doctor checks on a patient in the morning.
transferReply: Did you sleep at all last night?
transferReplyJapanese: 昨夜は少しでも眠れましたか？
nuance: Use it only in negatives and questions, usually at the end. Not at all is also a polite answer to thank you.
nuanceJapanese: 否定文と疑問文だけで使い、ふつう文末に置く。Not at all は thank you への丁寧な返事にもなる。

meaning: At the beginning, before things changed.
cue: Talk about learning to drive.
reply: At first I was scared, but now I enjoy driving.
replyJapanese: 最初は怖かったのですが、今は運転が楽しいです。
transferCue: Describe how you met your best friend.
transferReply: We didn't talk much at first.
transferReplyJapanese: 最初のうちは、あまり話しませんでした。
nuance: It suggests that things changed later, so but often follows. For the first item in a list, say first or firstly, not at first.
nuanceJapanese: あとで状況が変わったことを含むので、but が続くことが多い。順序の「まず」には first や firstly を使い、at first は使わない。

meaning: Finally, after a long wait.
cue: Your train arrives after a long delay.
reply: At last, our train is here!
replyJapanese: やっと電車が来ましたね！
transferCue: Tell a friend that your exams have finished.
transferReply: My exams are over at last.
transferReplyJapanese: やっと試験が終わりました。
nuance: It shows relief after waiting. For the last item in a list, say lastly or finally, not at last.
nuanceJapanese: 待ったあとの安心を表す。順序の「最後に」には lastly や finally を使い、at last は使わない。

meaning: Not less than a number or amount.
cue: A visitor asks how far the castle is.
reply: It takes at least an hour on foot.
replyJapanese: 歩くと少なくとも1時間はかかります。
transferCue: A doctor gives advice on a hot day.
transferReply: Drink at least two litres of water a day.
transferReplyJapanese: 1日に少なくとも2リットルの水を飲んでください。
nuance: Put it before the number. At most is the opposite. It also softens bad news: at least nobody was hurt.
nuanceJapanese: 数の前に置く。反対は at most。悪い知らせをやわらげるときにも使う（at least nobody was hurt）。

meaning: Immediately, without waiting.
cue: A manager hears about a water leak.
reply: Call the plumber at once, please.
replyJapanese: すぐに配管工を呼んでください。
transferCue: An old friend phones after many years.
transferReply: I recognised her voice at once.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女の声だとすぐに分かりました。
nuance: Slightly formal and firm; in everyday talk right away or straight away is more common. It can also mean at the same time.
nuanceJapanese: やや改まった強い言い方で、日常会話では right away や straight away が多い。「同時に」の意味にもなる。

meaning: Now, at this time.
cue: A caller asks to speak to your manager.
reply: She's not at her desk at the moment.
replyJapanese: ただいま席を外しております。
transferCue: A friend asks what you are reading.
transferReply: I'm not reading anything at the moment.
transferReplyJapanese: 今のところ、何も読んでいません。
frame: Be doing something at the moment
nuance: Keep at and the: in the moment has a different meaning. It suggests the situation may change soon.
nuanceJapanese: at と the を変えない（in the moment は別の意味）。状況がまもなく変わるかもしれないという含みがある。
